data.title: TB regimens for cutaneous tuberculosis
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Standard short-course antituberculous chemotherapy (India NTEP)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Standard short-course antituberculous chemotherapy (India NTEP)

## Mechanism of action
- Combination of bactericidal (H, R, Z) and resistance-preventing (E) drugs
- Intensive phase kills the bulk of bacilli; continuation phase kills persisters

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- All forms of cutaneous TB: lupus vulgaris, scrofuloderma, tuberculosis verrucosa cutis, orificial TB, metastatic tuberculous abscess, miliary TB of skin
- Tuberculids (papulonecrotic tuberculid, lichen scrofulosorum, erythema induratum) — when an active TB focus is found or empirically
- Therapeutic trial in suspected cutaneous TB (response in 4–6 weeks supports the diagnosis)

## Dose & formulations
- India NTEP (daily regimen, new patients): intensive phase 2 months HRZE, continuation phase 4 months HRE (ethambutol continued) — total 6 months, fixed-dose combinations by weight band
- Extend continuation phase for extensive/scrofuloderma or slow responders (total 9–12 months, by physician decision)
- Drug-resistant TB: per NTEP drug-resistant guidelines (rapid molecular testing, bedaquiline-based regimens)

## Adverse effects
- Hepatotoxicity (H, R, Z) — commonest reason to interrupt
- Cutaneous drug reactions to ATT are common: morbilliform rash, lichenoid eruptions, DRESS, SJS/TEN — reintroduce drugs one by one after recovery

## Contraindications
- See individual drugs

## Monitoring
- Monthly clinical review; LFT if symptoms or risk; notification to NTEP (Nikshay); HIV test

## Pregnancy & lactation
First-line drugs (HRZE) are used in pregnancy; avoid streptomycin.

## Viva points
- 2HRZE + 4HRE daily (NTEP)
- Therapeutic trial — response by 4–6 weeks
- Reintroduction of ATT after cutaneous reactions

## Note on sources
Khopkar describes the older DOTS (thrice-weekly) regimen; India now uses daily fixed-dose combinations (NTEP). The current regimen is given here.

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7 (Regimens, DOTS); NTEP guidelines; Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
